title: 영어브리핑_2026-11-20
korean_summary: 금요일 핵심: 본사 실적·예상손익 회신(먼저 회계장 사유 확인), 근로계약 처리안 인사 확인 후 보고, 주간 보고 2건.
paragraphs: Good morning, Anthony. Today is Friday, November twentieth. It is the last full working day of this week. Take a deep breath and enjoy the ride.

Here is the plan for the next twenty minutes. There are eight parts. Part one is this opening. Part two is the top three tasks for today. Part three is the reports you need to collect. Part four is the replies you owe. Part five is your schedule and deadlines. Part six is English review. Part seven is a short role-play. Part eight is the closing.
Let's begin.
Part two. Top three for today.
Number one. The head office report on October results and the forecast.

What is it? A head office manager asked for two things. First, the October results. Second, the forecast from November to February. The deadline is today, Friday. Your calendar also has an all-day reminder called profit and loss report.

Why does it matter? This is a head office deadline, and my director will look at it before it goes out. The forecast also depends on the CM plan. CM means cutting and making, our sewing fee. Yesterday, the chief accountant sent a new CM plan. You did not approve it yet. You asked her to give a reason for each style. One buyer's tax CM went down a lot, but the actual CM almost did not change. And three other styles had no CM cut in the new plan.

What is your first action? Open your inbox and look for the chief accountant's answer first. If the reasons make sense, approve the plan and finish the forecast. If she has not answered, call her before nine. Then show the draft to my director before lunch, and send it to the head office manager in the afternoon.
Number two. A worker's contract that ends tomorrow.

What is it? Head office said the CEO wants a way without an indefinite-term contract for one sewing worker. Her current contract ends tomorrow, Saturday. Yesterday you asked the HR staff to check each option under the labor law. You asked for her answer by November twenty-first.
Why does it matter? The contract ends tomorrow. If we choose the wrong option, it can become a legal risk. The law protects some workers strongly, so we must be careful.

What is your first action? Talk to the HR staff in the morning. Ask her which options are possible, and which law articles support them. Then report the safe option to my director today, and reply to the head office manager. Do not wait until Saturday afternoon.
Number three. The Friday weekly reports.

What is it? Every Friday you send two regular reports. The first is the weekly cash flow report to head office finance. The second is the outsourcing usage report to my director. The shipping manager should update the customs part of the outsourcing file by Friday morning.

Why does it matter? These are fixed weekly reports. Head office expects them every Friday. Also, this week the cash flow has a change. Yesterday you asked the accounting staff to use the second version of the Tet budget. Tet is the Lunar New Year holiday, and the payment dates changed.

What is your first action? At ten, check that the shipping manager updated the outsourcing file. Then check that the accounting staff used the new Tet budget in the cash flow. Send both reports in the afternoon.
Part three. Reports to collect.

First, the chief accountant. You need her reason for each style in the CM plan. You also need news about the VAT refund. VAT means value added tax. The tax office approved the refund yesterday. The money may arrive today or on Monday. Here is a sentence you can use. "Could you let me know where the VAT refund stands, and when the money will arrive?"

Second, the accounting staff. She is fixing the monthly file that compares management profit and tax profit. You asked her to write the difference amount and the reason for each account. The amounts should add up to the total difference. Here is a sentence for her. "Please make sure that the amounts add up to the difference. Otherwise, we cannot explain it to head office."

Third, the compliance officer. There are two topics. The first is the June electrical work. The contractor changed the parts on the wrong breaker. They worked on the boiler breaker, not the air compressor. They promised to fix it today and install a temperature sensor. The second topic is the December inspection. Two companies will send new quotes with the same scope as the current contractor. Here is a sentence for the compliance officer. "Please send me photos after they fix the correct breaker, before we make the payment."

Fourth, the HR manager. You sent her the draft salary evaluation plan for next year. You asked for comments on three points. She also has the KPI form draft, due today. KPI means key performance indicator. Here is a sentence for her. "Could you send me your comments on the evaluation plan and the KPI form by the end of today?"

Fifth, the warehouse manager. You asked her for training material for new warehouse staff. Many new staff leave early, so this matters. Her deadline is today. Here is a sentence. "Could you send me the onboarding checklist for new staff today, as we discussed?"

Sixth, the shipping manager. You asked her for the Incoterms for each buyer and ship mode. Incoterms are the trade rules that show who pays for what. You also want to know if the forwarder charged the airport security check fee for the last hanging garment shipment. Here is a sentence. "Apart from the Incoterms list, could you confirm whether the forwarder charged the security fee this time?"
Part four. Replies I owe.

First, the purchasing staff. She sent the air conditioner quotation for the sample room. The price includes VAT, and the warranty is two years. One supplier agreed to lower the installation fee. Remember, the purchasing staff often misses deadlines, so reply quickly and give a clear date. Your first sentence can be: "Thank you for the quotation. Before we decide, please confirm that all suppliers quoted the same model and capacity."

Second, the HR manager about work accident costs. She answered your four questions yesterday. She gave the name of the hospital we use for serious injuries and accidents after six in the evening. Now you can set the new process. Your first sentence can be: "Thank you for the details. Based on your answers, here is the process we will follow from now on."

Third, the purchase request from the accounting staff. A new purchase request arrived in the groupware yesterday evening. Review it and approve it, or ask questions. Your first sentence can be: "Could you tell me what this purchase request is for, and attach the quotation?"

Fourth, the new warehouse clerk. She sent her daily report again with more details, as you asked. She added style numbers and quantities. A short thank-you will keep her motivated. Your first sentence can be: "Thank you. This report is much clearer. Please keep this format every day."
Fifth, check if you already answered the payroll staff about the short-term worker payroll. Payment must be made before November twenty-fourth. If not, reply today.
Part five. Schedule and deadlines.

Today, Friday. All day, the profit and loss report to head office. At twelve noon, a thirty-minute online meeting about the HR system organization chart and headcount update. Also the weekly cash flow report, and the outsourcing report to my director. Today is also your monthly check of the shipping cost ledger for October.

Tomorrow, Saturday, November twenty-first. One worker's contract ends. The HR staff's legal check is due. The sales department debit closing is also due. Debit means the cost we charge to head office.
Monday, November twenty-third. The debit approval document in the groupware. The VAT refund may arrive.
Tuesday, November twenty-fourth. The collective bargaining agreement expires, and it is the culture day.
Part six. English review.
Let's review some expressions from this week. Listen, then say them with me.

The expression is "quantify." It means to show something in numbers. For example, "Please quantify each task in your daily report: how many rolls and yards you checked." Now say it with me. Please quantify each task in your daily report.
... ... ...
One more time. Please quantify each task.
... ... ...

The expression is "itemize." It means to write each cost on a separate line. For example, "Please ask the suppliers to itemize the pump and installation costs." Now say it with me. Please ask the suppliers to itemize the costs.
... ... ...
One more time. Please itemize the costs.
... ... ...

The expression is "consolidate." It means to put many things together into one. For example, "The clinic will consolidate the month's medical costs and bill us once." Now say it with me. The clinic will consolidate the costs and bill us once.
... ... ...
One more time. Consolidate the costs.
... ... ...

The expression is "Apart from this, is there anything else that..." We use it to ask if there is more. For example, "Apart from this list, is there anything else that was sent under our tax code?" Now say it with me. Apart from this list, is there anything else?
... ... ...
One more time. Apart from this list, is there anything else?
... ... ...

The expression is "From now on, let's make it a rule that..." It sets a new rule. For example, "From now on, let's make it a rule that the two loading documents go to the shipping team within two days." Now say it with me. From now on, let's make it a rule that we send it within two days.
... ... ...
One more time. From now on, let's make it a rule.
... ... ...

The expression is "cross-check." It means to compare with another document to check. For example, "Who cross-checks the trucking invoice against the booking?" Now say it with me. Who cross-checks the invoice against the booking?
... ... ...
One more time. Cross-check the invoice.
... ... ...

The expression is "My understanding is that... Please correct me if I'm wrong." It is a polite way to check facts. For example, "My understanding is that our team books the trucks directly. Please correct me if I'm wrong." Now say it with me. My understanding is that our team books the trucks. Please correct me if I'm wrong.
... ... ...
One more time. Please correct me if I'm wrong.
... ... ...

The expression is "defer." It means to move a decision or purchase to later. For example, "Disk prices are high now, so we will defer the replacement until the drive fails." Now say it with me. We will defer the replacement.
... ... ...
One more time. Defer the replacement.
... ... ...

The expression is "Given that..., we will..." It gives a reason, then a decision. For example, "Given that the total cost is high, we will replace only some drives this year." Now say it with me. Given that the cost is high, we will replace only some drives.
... ... ...
One more time. Given that the cost is high.
... ... ...

The expression is "Could you let me know where something stands?" It asks about progress. For example, "Could you let me know where the interlining upload stands?" Now say it with me. Could you let me know where the upload stands?
... ... ...
One more time. Where does it stand?
... ... ...

The expression is "Please make sure that... Otherwise..." It gives a check and the risk. For example, "Please make sure that the mainboard is the right version. Otherwise, the memory will not fit." Now say it with me. Please make sure that it is the right version. Otherwise, it will not fit.
... ... ...
One more time. Please make sure. Otherwise, it will not fit.
... ... ...

The expression is "The main reason why... is that..." It explains the biggest cause. For example, "The main reason new staff leave early is that the job is hard to learn." Now say it with me. The main reason new staff leave early is that the job is hard to learn.
... ... ...
One more time. The main reason is that the job is hard to learn.
... ... ...

The expression is "What would you suggest we do if...?" It asks for advice on a problem. For example, "What would you suggest we do if a new sewer is below grade C after three days?" Now say it with me. What would you suggest we do if the quote is too high?
... ... ...
One more time. What would you suggest we do?
... ... ...
Part seven. Role-play.
Today you will talk with the chief accountant about the new CM plan. Listen to the dialogue first.
Anthony: Good morning. Did you check my questions about the new CM plan?
Chief accountant: Yes. I sent you an answer this morning.
Anthony: Thank you. My understanding is that the actual CM did not change for that style. Please correct me if I'm wrong.
Chief accountant: That's right. The actual CM is almost the same.
Anthony: Then why did the tax CM go down so much?
Chief accountant: The buyer changed the order plan. We moved some cost to other months.
Anthony: I see. Could you show me the calculation for each month? I need to explain it to head office.
Chief accountant: Sure. I will add a sheet with the calculation.
Anthony: Good. And for the other three styles, the old plan had a CM cut. The new plan has no cut. Why?
Chief accountant: Those orders are new. The CM cut was only for the old orders.
Anthony: Okay. Please make sure that the file shows old orders and new orders separately. Otherwise, head office will be confused.
Chief accountant: No problem. I can send it by ten.
Anthony: Great. Given that the head office deadline is today, I need it by ten at the latest. Unless I hear otherwise, I will approve the plan after I check the file.
Chief accountant: Understood. I will send it soon.
Now let's practice two key sentences.

First sentence. My understanding is that the actual CM did not change. Please correct me if I'm wrong.
... ... ...
One more time. Please correct me if I'm wrong.
... ... ...

Second sentence. Please make sure that the file shows old orders and new orders separately. Otherwise, head office will be confused.
... ... ...
One more time. Please make sure. Otherwise, head office will be confused.
... ... ...
Part eight. Closing.
Here is the one thing to remember today. Get the chief accountant's reasons early, finish the forecast, and send it to head office before the end of the day.
Also, settle the worker's contract option with the HR staff before Saturday. And send the two Friday reports.
You have done a lot this week. Finish strong today, and enjoy your weekend. See you on Monday.
